script: How much money do teams that WIN their Champions League QUALIFIER GET? So the Champions League is the biggest club competition in football, and just to get into it, teams that didn't clinch an auto-qualification have to survive a brutal qualifying stage where clubs battle through these play-off rounds every year hoping to reach the league phase, where thirty-six teams get in. But the way clubs actually get paid for this is nothing like what you'd expect. When a team actually wins their qualifier, they don't get handed a special prize for winning that specific match, and there's no bonus for beating your opponent in that tie, because the reward is something much bigger. Well, financially at least. By winning, you unlock a spot in the league phase, and that's where UEFA's money machine kicks in, since every one of those thirty-six clubs gets a guaranteed 18.62 million euros, which is around 16 million pounds. That money comes split into a 17.87 million euro down payment and a 150 thousand euro balance later. But one missed result in that qualifier can cost a club almost everything. Teams that lose in the play-offs and miss the league phase walk away with just 4.29 million euros. So one result decides whether you pocket 4 million or nearly 19.
